name: mcp-retrieval-then-compare
procedure: pull the reference docs through MCP, compare them against the local implementation, report
why:
Sessions 1-4 are all coding sessions that end in a commit. Work done through tools has no marker by nature, and this is the shape the pipeline claims to support: `trim_leading_exploration`'s docstring argues that an MCP retrieval is step one of a method, not the search that found the task, and exempts it from trimming for exactly this reason. One task — pull the docs, compare, report — so the ground truth is one episode and no markers.

Recorded with `adk-docs` rather than Confluence: Confluence MCP is wired into the backend agent, not exposed to Claude Code, which the session established itself. The server does not matter to what is under test — `is_read_only` classifies MCP by verb prefix and the trim exempts any `mcp__` call.
history:
CLOSED. The MCP exemption held all along; a second rule defeated it.

  ep0  4 work steps, all MCP retrieval, ended_by=prompt, flagged=True   DROPPED
  ep1  6 work steps, no MCP,            ended_by=session-end            banked

`trim_leading_exploration` never got to apply its exemption, because a flagging rule discarded any episode whose every substantive step only looked at things — and a pure retrieval is exactly that. The banked entry was the comparison alone, titled after the second prompt, with nothing recording where the reference material came from. The half the procedure exists for was the half thrown away.

The count was right throughout, so only `must_contain` could see it. That is the assertion this fixture was recorded to make.

Fixed by `_absorb_read_only_preamble`: reading that precedes work is folded into it, and the all-read-only flag is gone. Its only justification was `reading-around` in `tests/benchmarks/cases.py`, hand-authored alongside the detector; this session is what it cost on real work. Absorbing is forward only — reading that ends a session still concludes nothing and is still flagged.

Under the judge this session was never broken: verdicts stop prompts from cutting, so there was one episode and the retrieval survived. The defect was on the vocabulary path, which is what runs when the local model is unreachable.
